text:
ana: FYI I just got a Snyk alert for CVE-2026-1987 impacting OpenSSL ECDSA path in libssl 3.1 on alpine:3.19-based slim images. Likely affects our backend-python and worker images. Can we triage impact + plan a patch/rebuild?
chris: thanks. quick question — do we know which runtime variants pull libssl 3.1? alpine:3.19 is the common one for our slim python images but some services use ubuntu-slim.
maria: I ran a `docker scan` on the latest prod tag earlier, same vuln flagged on two images: `redwood/backend-python:prod-latest` and `redwood/worker:prod-latest`. Both are based on `python:3.11-alpine3.19`.
sam: marking severity: probably high for services doing ECDSA TLS or signing. If only server TLS stacks validate, risk may be lower but we should assume exploitable.
nana (typo correction): oops ignore
chris: action proposal: 1) build patched images on alpine:3.20 with OpenSSL 3.2 if available OR 2) rebuild against musl with distro backport for libssl 3.1-1+hotfix. 3) sign images, deploy canary to staging, monitor. Which path is faster?
maria: 1) is fastest if alpine:3.20 packages include OpenSSL 3.2 — I'll check package repo. 2) will need more testing.
sec-bot: [alert] CVE-2026-1987 severity=High vector=Network component=openssl posted_by=snyk
chris: also: we need to consider our image signing + key rotation. If we rebuild, images must be cosigned and pushed. Do we have an HSM/KMS-backed key available for cosign?
maria: We have an AWS KMS key `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd` used for CI signing in staging but not enabled for prod pipeline. I can enable with a short rotation window.
sam: I can run a canary pipeline for the rebuilt images. Plan: build -> sign with KMS (staging key) -> push to staging tag -> deploy to staging canary hosts -> smoke tests (tls handshake + attestation) -> promote. How long do we think? 4-6 hours once build is green?
a na: (ignore second accidental message)
chris: smoke tests to include: `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -curves secp256r1` and an ECDSA signing verification flow for our internal signing endpoints. Add `otlp` traces for TLS handshake errors.
maria: quick package check: alpine 3.20 main repo shows `openssl-3.2.0-r1` which includes the upstream patch. I'll start rebuilding python:3.11-alpine3.20 variants today.
sam: two operational asks: 1) can we gate prod promotion on audit log spike/no regressions? 2) can sec enable image-signing KMS in prod pipeline?
chris: +1 on gating by audit logs. Also need RBAC check: only CI bots and release engineers should be allowed to sign/promote images. Maria, can you create a short RBAC policy for the KMS key and cosign principal?
maria: yes — I'll draft a policy granting kms:Sign to `ci/cosign-role` and `release-engineers` group, deny to others. Will post the policy in this thread when done.
sec-bot: [info] created ticket SEC-5421: "Alpine OpenSSL CVE-2026-1987 rebuild + KMS signing" assigned=chris priority=high
chris: timeline: maria starts builds now, sam runs canary tomorrow morning (09:00 PT), monitoring window 2 hours, if green we promote to prod at ~13:00 with on-call on-standby. Any blockers?
a na: removing typo messages
maria: policy draft posted to `#eng-security` (short link) — confirms KMS key policy and cosign IAM role. Also will enable kms key rotation every 90 days.
sam: I'll prepare a smoke test script and share a small runbook for on-call: checks, rollback tag, and how to revoke signed images if needed.
chris: please include steps to revoke key from KMS (in case of compromise) and how to mark images untrusted in our registry.
maria: noted.
na na: (typo again)
chris: ok assigning owners: maria = build + KMS policy, sam = canary + runbook, chris = incident coordinator + promote. I'll update SEC-5421 with these owners.
na na: (final remove)
sec-bot: [info] SEC-5421 updated owners: maria,sam,chris
maria: started first build: `docker build --pull -t redwood/backend-python:alpine3.20-patched .` — build logs look ok, openssl 3.2 present. Pushing signed tag to staging now.
sam: received artifact, starting canary deploy to `staging-canary-02`. Running smoke tests.
sam: smoke tests: tls handshake OK, ECDSA signing verification OK, no regressions in unit tests. CPU/memory within expected. No error spikes in traces after 30m.
chris: thanks. schedule prod promotion at 12:45 PT, on-call @oncall-backend will be paged at start and monitor for 60m. If any TLS errors revert to last-signed tag `redwood/backend-python:prod-2026-03-12-signed` and revoke key if we see signature issues.
maria: prod signing KMS enabled, RBAC attached, rotation scheduled. I've documented the IAM policy in the ticket.
sec-bot: [resolved] CVE-2026-1987 mitigated in prod via upgrade to openssl 3.2 and image redeploy. ticket=SEC-5421 closed
chris: great work team :thumbsup: — will follow up with a short postmortem + checklist for future base image CVEs."
